account:
Today I have been following my appointments, though several have run late, and investigating a vague story about changes to the bridge or port. So far I have no firsthand evidence that any such change exists. At tea, neighbour finally explained that Townsfolk 23 supplied the vague bakery story, naming baker and freight as present. Neighbour personally witnessed no changes. Freight told neighbour this morning that ferry service was available, while baker told neighbour there was no newly confirmed news. Secretary separately reported that baker described ordinary freight business and had no firsthand evidence of crossing changes. Townsfolk 23 and freight are therefore sensible people to question directly; I do not yet know what the alleged discussion was for.

There is ordinary grain and bread activity: I saw 128 hay bales at the mill stall, but have not inspected its storage or deliveries or identified its keeper. Secretary says baker does not know who manages it. A villager reported freight carrying a sack of bread at the inn, and another reported baker carrying wheat at the bakery. Those reports could fit routine provisioning and deliveries; they do not establish a secret undertaking.

Builder reported no specific visible defects on his bridge and public-lighting rounds, with no purchases, repairs, or charges. His inspection was visual only, not a structural survey or nighttime lighting test. I funded two writable books through secretary to record his findings and town business.

One unresolved administrative matter is the council correspondence. Secretary said there were no council letters in hand and asked where they were kept. I saw secretary take a written book from the appointments chest at 14:31, but do not know which book it was. Freight also gave secretary a written book yesterday; I do not know its contents. These exchanges might be ordinary administration, not evidence of concealment. I have just returned to the office and can see secretary and builder. I want to obtain the written records and clarify the correspondence, then trace the crossing rumor to firsthand sources rather than mistake hearsay for a confirmed plan.
